newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off on Dow drop but trade weak.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off on Dow drop but trade weak.

text.p: Brazilian shares shed early gains to edge down at the close, weighed down by Wall Street, but trade was thin as many investors stayed away to await a vote this week by Brazil's Congress on re-election, brokers said.

"The Dow is dragging all Latin American markets down," one dealer told Reuters. "The bolsa was up but the Dow fell when they raised interest rates in the U.S. and that weighed on us." The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares ended off 0.01 percent at 77,591 points on volume of 316.8 million reais ($304.6 million).

Brokers said trade was down sharply from recent sessions as many investors opted to stay away until Congress' lower house votes later this week on President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's re-election amendment. The bolsa was up in weak morning trade after news reports said the Chamber of Deputies would cast an initial vote on re-election by Wednesday. But those gains were swept away when the Dow began sliding.

Despite the Bovespa's close, some major blue chips ended higher, including benchmark Telebras. Telebras preferred rose 0.34 percent to close at 89.00 reais while its voting common ended up 0.85 percent at 82.90 reais.
State mining firm Cia Vale do Rio Doce closed 0.44 percent higher at 22.90 reais while Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras ended flat at 27.90 reais.
Among other blue chips, state power holding Eletrobras closed down 1.17 percent to end at 424.00 reais.
The decline in Eletrobras led an overall decline in power shares.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid shares closed down 0.27 percent to end at 2,293 points.
Among other power losers was Minas Gerais state's Cemig, which fell 0.67 percent at 44.30 reais.
Brokers said Brazilian stock have bright prospects but may repeat the performance Tuesday as local markets await an influx of foreign capital after Congress' expected vote.
